source.title: Sparse components distinguish visual pathways & their alignment to neural networks
source.authors: Ammar I Marvi; Nancy Kanwisher; Meenakshi Khosla

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares component response profiles across visual models, a different-method test of whether interpretable features recur across models. It does not sweep model scale or directly compare model-to-model representational distances.
record.gate_note: The paper's brain-to-DNN alignment measurements concern a related but different comparison from the claim versions, so they are recorded with versions ["none"]. The model-component result bears on V5. Other background claims about alignment are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study's own NMF decomposition of seven vision DNNs bears qualitatively on V5. It found shared category motifs across AlexNet, ResNet-50 and ViT trained with supervised and self-supervised objectives. It is a side observation in a new setting (NSD images, Bayesian NMF components), not a method aimed at the convergence question, so T3 rather than T2. The main results are brain-to-DNN alignment, which no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that rotation-invariant metrics (encoding, RSA) hide stream differences that SCA reveals. They say DNNs share tuning axes with ventral-stream neurons, and the weak dorsal/lateral fit shows limits of current objectives and data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Bayesian NMF components and Sparse Component Alignment, alongside encoding and RSA, for brain-to-DNN comparisons and qualitative comparisons of model component profiles; it does not measure model-to-model convergence or scale. Not a replication of the cited convergence methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Brain-to-DNN alignment differs across linear encoding, RSA, and SCA; SCA gives markedly lower alignment for dorsal and lateral streams than for ventral.

fits_no_version.finding: Brain-to-DNN alignment depends on the metric. Linear encoding and RSA show similar alignment across the ventral, dorsal and lateral streams. SCA shows ventral alignment (r=0.187) well above lateral (0.047) and dorsal (0.058), which approach the untrained baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-trained DNNs align with the ventral visual stream along shared tuning axes, and rotation-invariant metrics mask weaker alignment to the dorsal and lateral streams.

record.problems: The model-component recurrence result is qualitative and does not report per-model feature matches or a quantitative cross-model similarity measure. The brain data come from four subjects; the text gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported alignment values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. The paper also reports component saliency correlations, behavioral alignment, and simulation results, but these do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no model-to-model similarity measure.
No vision-language models or paired caption data.
No mapping, stitching or interchangeability test between models.
No quantitative cross-model matching of individual units, components, circuits or SAE features. The similarity is judged only by eye from top-image response profiles (Fig. 10).
Metric dependence is shown only for brain-to-model alignment (encoding vs RSA vs SCA), not for model-to-model convergence.
No test of whether model-to-model alignment plateaus or of what causes it. All models share ImageNet-1k training data.

record.verdict_notes: Removed the reader's V5 limits_scope label. The lack of quantitative feature matching is an untested part, not a shown limitation. All seven models share the ImageNet-1k training data, so the shared motifs cannot separate shared data from convergence. The V5 evidence rests on one qualitative sentence and Fig. 10.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no measurement of representational similarity between independently trained models.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language models.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test between models.
The study reports qualitative similarity of component response profiles, not recurrence of precisely matched neurons, circuits, or SAE features, nor causal tests of shared features.
The study compares alignment metrics for brain-to-model alignment, not metric or input dependence of model-to-model convergence.
No test of whether model-to-model alignment plateaus or is explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: DNNs (models tested; aggregate)

rows.operation_detail: Compared NMF-derived component response profiles across tested models.

conditions.value: AlexNet, ResNet-50, and ViT models; supervised and self-supervised objectives; untrained AlexNet also examined

rows.measure: Qualitative similarity and interpretable category motifs in component response profiles across models
rows.value: Pre-trained models showed motifs including faces, scenes, words, and animals; the paper states that variations in training objective and architecture did not produce notably different response profiles in the tested models. Untrained models appeared selective for low-level features.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative result; the text does not give per-model feature matches or quantitative cross-model similarity values. The finding supports recurrence of broad motifs, but does not establish that identical individual features or circuits recur.
rows.check: Change state from partial to observed. The text says pre-trained models shared motifs (faces, scenes, words, animals), and that objective and architecture 'did not produce notably different response profiles.' That is the effect as stated, though only qualitatively. The lack of quantitative or per-feature matching is an untested part, not partial support. Untrained models' low-level selectivity is not a learned-model comparison. Subject should list the six pre-trained models of Fig. 10.

relationships.condition: Six ImageNet-1k pre-trained vision DNNs (AlexNet, ResNet-50 supervised/MoCo-v2/SimCLR, ViT supervised/DINO), NMF components on NSD images
relationships.reason: r1: the components show shared category motifs, and the authors state architecture and objective did not notably change response profiles. The evidence is qualitative only.
relationships.display_finding: Components displayed shared category motifs, with no notable qualitative change in response profiles across architectures and objectives.
